title.narrative: Mubaderoom 3

description.narrative:
In line with the objectives of Plan International Jordan's Centre of Excellence, the project aims to promote and strengthen social entrepreneurship beyond the project's duration. To foster long-term sustainability, the project will:
- Cross-country collaboration: The project will be exemplary in fostering cross-country collaboration, strengthening regional localization efforts, and guaranteeing sustainable continuation and learnings harvesting. - Research and Learning Hub: Conducting research to better understand the challenges and opportunities for youth economic empowerment in the Lebanon and the region, including a monitoring and evaluation mechanism to assess the effectiveness and impact of youth economic empowerment interventions. - Program Design and Innovation: Supporting the development and implementation of regional innovative programs and initiatives that directly contribute to youth economic empowerment. This may involve providing technical assistance and guidance to projects that demonstrate potential for sustainable economic outcomes for youth.

Lebanon faces a deepening and multifaceted crisis, marked by economic collapse, political paralysis, and a growing humanitarian emergency. As of late 2024, approximately 75% of the population lives in multidimensional poverty, with many unable to meet basic needs for food, healthcare, and shelter. Among Syrian refugees, the situation is even more dire, with nine out of ten households living in extreme poverty. Youth unemployment remains critically high (47%), exacerbating social tension and economic exclusion. At the same time, Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) which account for more than 90% of registered businesses and employ around 50% of the workforce have been severely affected. The situation further deteriorated in 2024 due to escalating conflict in South Lebanon, Beirut, and Mount Lebanon, which significantly disrupted infrastructure, displaced populations, and strained already fragile systems. An estimated one million people were internally displaced, altering demographic patterns and placing pressure on local economies, labour markets, and public services.

SUMMARY: Between April 2024 and September 2025, Mubaderoon III aims to build on and share the knowledge gained throughout the Mubaderoon I and Mubaderoon II projects carried out in Jordan from 2019 to 2023. It brings proven models of social entrepreneurship and youth economic empowerment to Lebanon, while adapting to the country’s complex and evolving context. By building the capacity of local actors and providing direct support to young entrepreneurs in Beirut, Mount Lebanon and Akkar, the project will generate sustainable, inclusive livelihoods and challenge entrenched gender inequalities. Plan Lebanon together with Plan Jordan's Centre of Excellence (CoE) for youth economic empowerment will support 300 youth (18-35 yrs) building entrepreneurial and employability skills and 70 with seed capital and technical assistance to develop innovative and sustainable businesses.

Since 2019, Lebanon has faced a severe socioeconomic and political crisis marked by high unemployment, inflation, a shortage of foreign currency, and communal tensions. The COVID-19 pandemic, Beirut port explosion, and Syrian refugee crisis have worsened the situation, leading the World Bank to label it one of the worst economic crises in modern history in 2021. The recent Gaza war has further impacted key sectors, heightening the risk of economic contraction. From a gender perspective, women face disproportionate impacts, with lower labor force participation (32.7% unemployment rate versus 28.4% for men), higher reliance on family for financial access, and a higher proportion of job losses compared to men. Lebanon hosts over two million refugees, with 815,000 Syrian and 500,000 Palestinian refugees registered. The ongoing crises deepen vulnerabilities, particularly affecting refugees and migrants. Around 60% of Syrian youth aged 15-24 are not in education, employment, or training.

The project will be implemented through a conflict sensitive, flexible, and community-based approach. Mubaderoon III addresses key barriers to youth economic participation by combining capacity building, seed funding, coaching, and market linkages. This integrated model enables young people to develop community-driven enterprises that foster economic resilience, social inclusion, and recovery, even in the face of ongoing instability.
Outcome 1: Building the capacity of Plan international Lebanon by leveraging the insights and methodology derived from Mubaderoon and similar projects Outcome 2: Strengthening local entrepreneurship ecosystem and expanding/creating social enterprises by providing: a) Social enterprises and youth with entrepreneurship skills and training to develop business plans and; b) seed funding and linkages to the labour market for selected youth and enterprises.

The project will benefit youth (aged 18–35) from Beirut, Akkar and Mount Lebanon with special focus on women and girls. For the social entrepreneurship pathway, the project we will support MSME business owners and early-stage and growing social Lebanese enterprises. The project will also work with Syrian refugees and vulnerable host community members to facilitate integration and improve livelihoods.

The project will include the following activities: • Develop gender-sensitive tools and curricula on youth entrepreneurship and social enterprises • Conduct Training of Trainers (ToT) for facilitators to deliver market relevant skills training • Establish a network of social entrepreneurs to foster collaboration and knowledge exchange • Facilitate knowledge and experience sharing through a knowledge-sharing platform, workshops, seminars, and peer learning • Train and coach 300 young people with entrepreneurship, employability, green and life skills with a focus on gender and inclusion, digital, green solutions/innovation, and labour rights. • Nurture advanced entrepreneurship skills among selected youth through business plan development training, mentorship, and pitch competitions • Conduct inter-gender dialogue sessions to discuss gender norms, harmful practices and barriers affecting women with parents/caregivers on gender • Distribution and monitoring of seed funding • Business Mentorship Programme • Establish and form linkages with the private sector to marketing of youth/enterprises production • Sensitization of the private sector on gender equality and inclusion and decent working conditions • Establish a network of social entrepreneurs to foster collaboration and knowledge exchange • Conduct research to assess the effectiveness of social entrepreneurship initiatives.
